stem: A town's transport office uses an exponential model for the number of electric scooters registered in the town. The model predicts that the number increases by \(44\%\) every 2 years. According to the model, the number increases by \(p\%\) each year. What is the value of \(p\)?
solution: A \(44\%\) increase every 2 years is a factor of 1.44 every 2 years.
If the yearly factor is \(r\), then \(r^{2} = 1.44\), so \(r = 1.2\).
A factor of 1.2 is a \(20\%\) increase each year, so \(p = 20\). (Not 22: half of \(44\%\) ignores compounding.)
verify:
r = symbols('r', positive=True)
sol = solve(Eq(r**2, Rational(144, 100)), r)
assert sol == [Rational(6, 5)]
p = (sol[0] - 1) * 100
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [p] == [20]
